Mostly a fix release, and the theme is **orbs that told the truth about
themselves**. 0.4.2 drew every local session as the one kind it was written for
— a terminal session that is running — and Claude Code has grown several kinds
that are not that. Fifteen breathing orbs on a machine nobody was working on
turned out to be fifteen real sessions the app did not understand, and clicking
most of them did nothing at all, silently.

Alongside that: timer-driven gateway orbs can now have a shape of their own or
none, and a Mac with nobody sitting at it can finally serve its sessions to your
other machines without someone walking over to press a button.

Still a beta. Remote Control is macOS-only, and the *Known limitations* section
below is not boilerplate — read it before relying on any of this.

## New: heartbeats and crons can have their own shape, or none

The arrange button used to gather every orb into one shape, and the only say you
had over the timer-driven ones was a single switch. Crons had no switch at all:
they always got an orb and it always joined the shape. A gateway with eight
heartbeat-enabled agents and three scheduled jobs put eleven orbs into the heart
that nobody was talking to, indistinguishable from the conversations that
matter.

**Heartbeat sessions** and **Cron sessions** are now separate settings with
three answers each:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Hidden** | No orb at all. |
| **With the chats** | An orb, gathered into the same shape as everything else. The default, and what the app has always done. |
| **Own shape** | An orb, gathered into a shape of its own, drawn beside your conversations rather than among them. |

Set both to *Own shape* and the arrange button draws three patterns side by side
— your chats, the heartbeats, the crons — each picking from the same six shapes.
The shapes get a share of the screen in proportion to how many orbs they hold,
and are drawn as one group centred on wherever you last dragged the arrangement,
so dragging still moves all of them together. Two shapes cannot land on top of
each other, which is why they are placed that way rather than each being given a
position of its own to lose.

**Nothing changes on upgrade.** If you had turned the old *Show heartbeat
sessions* switch off, that becomes *Hidden*; on — or never touched — becomes
*With the chats*. Crons always joined the one shape, which is what *With the
chats* means. Both settings live in **Settings → OpenClaw**, which only appears
once *Show OpenClaw agents* is on.

## New: a Mac that serves other machines unattended

The live mirror of a session is served by the Claude Buddy on that session's own
machine, and in 0.4.2 every path that brought that machine's relay up was a
person's gesture *on that machine*. A headless server — the real case was a Mac
mini whose sessions a laptop wanted to mirror — could therefore never serve: no
one is there to press anything, and SSH reaches none of the three triggers.

**Settings → Other machines** gains **Start serving at launch** (off by
default). Pair it with *Stop the relay after: Never* and the machine serves from
boot. Managing a headless Mac is then `settings.json` over SSH plus a relaunch.

Two fixes make that actually work on a real headless machine, and both were
found on one:

- **It serves while the screen is locked.** The app waits for the display to
  unlock before starting its UI, for a good reason, and the relay was waiting
  behind it — so on a mini whose screen never unlocks, the relay started exactly
  once all day, on the one launch that happened to follow a screen-sharing
  session. Every other launch sat parked in the unlock poll, alive and doing
  nothing. The relay now starts before the wait, and a locked machine answers
  "which sessions do you have" from a windowless snapshot instead of
  answering "none".
- **The relay finds its own status file under claude 2.1.251.** That version
  stopped handing the bridge's private `TMPDIR` through to hooks, so the file
  that signals "the relay is up" landed in the machine's real temp directory
  while the bridge watched an empty one — timing out at 45 seconds and tearing
  down a perfectly healthy session. Every fresh relay start lost this way, which
  killed the mirror on any machine whose relay restarted after upgrading.

## Fixed: orbs for sessions nobody was in

The headline bug, and the reason most of this release exists.

- **Parked background jobs are drawn as parked.** A background job runs inside a
  pooled worker that is deliberately kept alive after the turn ends, so "the
  process is alive" says almost nothing — and its hook writes the same `idle` a
  job mid-turn writes. The daemon knew the difference all along; the app read
  the field and threw it away. A parked orb is now drawn at 45% opacity, taken
  off the pulse roster, and wears a gear badge. Colour is identity, fill is
  state, and opacity and stillness are now presence.
- **Right-click gains *Dismiss this orb* and *End this session*** — hidden, not
  greyed, for the sessions they cannot serve.
- **Status files get swept.** Nothing but the graceful-exit hook had ever
  deleted one, so a Ctrl+C'd session's file stayed for good and a finished job's
  stayed *and could never be caught*, its worker being alive by design. The scan
  now sweeps a file after ten minutes of evidence its session is over.
- **Orbs with neither a terminal nor a transcript are not drawn at all**, and a
  session whose name the hook never caught now gets it read off its transcript
  instead of showing blank.
- **A backgrounded turn no longer leaves a husk behind**, or the duplicate orb
  that came with it.
- **Background jobs under a second account are found.** `claude agents` answers
  for one config directory and the daemon is per-account, and the app asked
  once. Every job under a second account was therefore classified as "not a job
  at all" and offered you terminal wording — for a job the daemon runs precisely
  so that no terminal has to hold it.

## Fixed: every orb click now produces a visible result (macOS)

*"Most of these dead orbs, when I try to go to terminal, they do nothing."* That
was literally true: six separate failures could run in a row for a team member
in a detached tmux socket, every one of them silent, and the last of them
reported to a stderr a bundled app has nowhere to show.

| Gesture | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Click a **teammate** orb | silently nothing | that teammate's own conversation, as a pane beside you |
| Click a **background** orb | silently nothing | its existing pane if there is one, otherwise `claude attach` split into the window you are already in |
| Right-click a background orb | — | **Open agents view**, focused if open |
| Click a session **already on screen** | a duplicate window, or nothing | nothing is created, and the orb flashes a halo so the gesture is visibly answered |

The chat panel was the last gesture still dead-ending: for a daemon-hosted
session it had no send path at all, and the note on a refused send said to reply
in the terminal — naming a window that does not exist.

**Windows click-access is not covered by this** and is tracked separately; see
*Known limitations*.

## Fixed: OpenClaw room messages went to the wrong agent

A message typed into a room panel went to the **alphabetically first** agent in
the channel and never reached the channel at all. In a real incident on 28
August, a reply meant for one agent in `#general` landed in an unrelated
outreach agent's session, which ran for three seconds and wrote nothing; the
intended recipient had no record of it and the channel showed nothing.

Two defects that compounded: the carrier session was picked by sorting names,
and the channel mirror was skipped whenever that session had fallen outside the
recency window — which the alphabetically-first agent, being uncorrelated with
recent activity, very often had. A room send now goes to the room, says so when
it cannot, and your own message is drawn as yours rather than as everyone else's.

## Fixed: a Claude Desktop profile that quietly became Default

Claude Desktop's own updater relaunches the bundle it just updated with neither
`--user-data-dir` nor the environment variable set, so a correctly-launched
profile became, after its first self-update, a second Chromium on the Default
profile's data directory — the concurrent-access case the whole profile feature
exists to prevent, arriving by the one route the launcher cannot reach. That
cannot be prevented from here (the updater is upstream, and rewriting it inside
a signed bundle would break the code identity the tinted clones depend on), so
the app now **detects it and says so**: a window wearing one profile's colour
and another profile's account is named rather than left to be discovered.

Profile selection itself also moved to Chromium's `--user-data-dir` switch
rather than the environment variable, tinted clones are rebuilt only when
actually behind, and the log-file probe reports what exists instead of trusting
`open(1)`.

## Fixed, smaller

- A team lead's window no longer swallows a click meant for one of its members.
- Clicking an orb attaches to the session that was clicked, not to whichever
  tmux session is busiest.
- The terminal is brought to the front, rather than only the pane to the top of
  its tmux session.
- This app's own relay no longer gets an orb of its own.
- A remote-control row taking over a background job no longer re-points that
  job's orb.
- A failure is reported once, not once per retry attempt.
- The settings screenshots capture the rows at the size the rows actually are,
  instead of clipping them.

## Under the hood

The coverage tooling now explains how to tell a coverage number from a
coverage-shaped one — three documented cases in this repo of a figure that read
as a regression and was not, only one of which was the code's fault. The
`merged 4 report(s)` self-check and a quiet process table are now written down
as the two things to check before quoting a number, because both have already
cost hours by being skipped.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.4.3-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.4.3-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.4.3-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `ClaudeBuddySpeech-0.4.3-beta-*.zip` assets are the optional high-quality
voice engine. **You do not download these yourself** — the app fetches the right
one when you turn the setting on. They are published here because that is where
it looks.

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers
every file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.4.2-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is unchanged, so
Automation permission and click-to-focus carry over.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one; it upgrades in place and leaves
your hook configuration alone.

No settings change meaning in this release. The heartbeat switch migrates to the
three-way setting as described above and your screen looks the same afterwards;
serving at launch is off until you turn it on.

Hooks are read once at session start, so **restart any open sessions** after
installing or updating. If you have a headless machine serving other machines,
its relay is the thing worth restarting — the status-file fix above only takes
effect on a fresh relay start.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click
**Install Claude Code Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications; nothing appears
in the Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave both checkboxes
ticked; tick **"Wire hooks for Claude Code running inside WSL"** too if you use
it.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook that Claude Code (and, for
Codex sessions, Codex) runs. Until it is wired in, the app starts and runs
correctly and shows **nothing at all**. The installers offer to wire it up; let
them. Existing settings are backed up first, and re-running repairs rather than
duplicating.

## Known limitations

- **The click-access fixes are macOS only.** The Windows equivalent is a
  separate ticket and is not in this release; a click on a terminal-less orb
  there behaves as it did in 0.4.2.
- **Remote Control is macOS only.** The relay is tmux-shaped; a Windows
  transport is tracked separately and is gated off rather than half-working.
- **Serve-at-launch on a genuinely headless machine is confirmed in its parts,
  not yet as one story.** The lock-screen path and the status-file location were
  both measured on the real Mac mini they were written for; the full loop —
  settings written over SSH, relaunch, the laptop's orb switching to the live
  mirror — is what these two fixes were built to enable and is being exercised
  on that hardware now.
- **claude 2.1.251 also gates a first relay run** behind per-config-context
  onboarding and a folder-trust dialog, both of which have to be answered by
  hand once on the serving machine. The bridge names the onboarding block when
  it sees it; automating the trust dialog is its own change and is not here.
- **The heartbeat's beat has never been watched moving on a screen.** It is
  asserted as a curve and rendered as a still frame; the label-matching branch
  is untested against a real payload, because the gateway's own heartbeat job
  sits behind a scope this app does not hold.
- **The Claude Desktop profile-drift detection reports, it does not repair.**
  The updater that causes it is upstream and takes no arguments this app can
  influence.
- **No streaming without a Buddy on the far side.** In messaging mode, a reply
  arrives when the remote session chooses to send it.
- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More info →
  Run anyway**. macOS builds are signed and notarized and open normally.
- A session killed with Ctrl+C at a permission prompt can still leave its orb
  stuck on amber. Right-click → *Reset this session to idle* clears it.

`docs/remote-control-findings.md`, `docs/claude-desktop-url-routing-findings.md`,
`docs/claude-desktop-user-data-dir-findings.md` and `docs/openclaw-findings.md`
record what was actually measured versus assumed, in more detail than fits here.
